items.evidence: Three independent dead causes, all javap-verified fresh against the 26.1.2 jar. (1) Dead dispatch: Class::Speleothem = "SpeleothemBlock" (level/classes.rs:215) gates five dispatch sites (place.rs:1156, shapes.rs:728, survive.rs:307, tick.rs:248, tick.rs:434), but there is NO SpeleothemBlock class in 26.1.2 - 0 matches in either jar; PointedDripstoneBlock extends Block directly (the 1.21.7 shape) and its prepared class chain is [PointedDripstoneBlock, Block], so no Speleothem arm ever fires. (2) Dead tag: speleothem_tag() reads #minecraft:speleothems, absent from 26.1.2 data (no tag file in the client jar, no BlockTags.SPELEOTHEMS field, no key in prepared block-tags.json), so speleothem_with / speleothem_is_tip / is_free_hanging_stalactite / speleothem_unmerged_tip are always false and falling.rs:55 spawn_falling_stalactite is tag-gated. (3) Missing link: prepared fields for pointed_dripstone is {} (no blockToGrowOn), so data.link is None and speleothem_grow's can_grow is always false; vanilla 26.1.2 PDB.canGrow hardcodes Blocks.DRIPSTONE_BLOCK + water source at above(2). Vanilla PDB bytecode has ZERO BlockTags references - all predicates are same-block. Observable: transfer, growth, cauldron fill, placement, updateShape, canSurvive (falls through to true, floating dripstone never breaks), scheduled tick, falling stalactite spawn all dead. NOT dead: fallOn stalagmite damage and trident break (name/data-keyed). The dead-code constants in speleothem.rs match vanilla exactly (growth 0.011377778, transfer 0.17578125/0.05859375, findTip max 11) but were not counted as passes. Reproduces pilot G6 + B11-G06 and 26.1.1 B1-G01; all in-scope files byte-identical to 26.1.1's.
items.title: Entire pointed-dripstone system dead (no SpeleothemBlock class, no #speleothems tag, no blockToGrowOn link)

items.evidence: Vanilla 26.1.2 FallingBlockEntity.tick runs the landing branch at the first water cell (onGround || inWater, where inWater = concrete powder && fluid is WATER tag, with a fast-fall clip check when the delta's length-squared exceeds 1.0, using ClipContext.Block.COLLIDER + ClipContext.Fluid.SOURCE_ONLY); the port's game/falling_blocks.rs fall_step has no concrete-powder water check at all and game/falling_damage.rs finish_falling_block always passes stuck_in_water=false, so powder sinks to the lakebed. The horizon-world landing branch itself (level/falling.rs falling_block_landed) matches vanilla, including the onLand replaced-state check - the fix is local to the client fall step. Carries over from pilot G2. Same defect as 26.2's B1-G02, 26.1's B1-G02 and 26.1.1's B1-G02; all in-scope files byte-identical to 26.1.1's.
items.title: Concrete powder falling into water does not solidify on contact

items.evidence: Vanilla 26.1.2 AbstractThrownPotion.onHitBlock gates on PotionContents.is(Potions.WATER) - Holder equality, NOT a tag (re-verified fresh; zero douses_fire references in the class). The port's game/splash_water.rs ships the 26.3 tag form: potion_in_tag(stack, "minecraft:douses_fire" / "hurts_water_sensitive_entities" / "extinguishes_entities" / "rehydrates_axolotls"), read from trades.potion_tags built from the prepared data's tags/potion directory (merchant.rs:488-489, 574). That directory contains ONLY tradeable.json in 26.1.2 (verified in the client jar - 1 potion tag file, 41 values - and in prepared data), so all four gates are always closed and no splash water ever dowses fire, hurts water-sensitive entities, extinguishes burning entities, or rehydrates axolotls. 26.2's file uses is_water_potion (Potions.WATER equality) and works. The downstream code matches vanilla exactly (dowse targets, dowseFire, the (4,2,4) box, dist^2<16, hurt 1.0 indirectMagic, axolotl +1800 air capped) but is unreachable. Reproduces B11-G13 and 26.1.1 B1-G03.
items.title: Splash water never douses fire / hurts / extinguishes / rehydrates (potion tags are 26.3-only)

items.evidence: Vanilla 26.1.2 EntityFluidInteraction is the 26.2 form (javap-verified fresh): trackerByFluid Map<TagKey, Tracker> with the current ON the tracker, no CurrentAccumulator class, update returns void; the eye check uses the PLAIN top (y + FluidState.getHeight). The port's horizon-world/src/entity_fluid.rs ships the 26.3 form (per-kind trackers + separate CurrentAccumulators, update returns Result<bool>) and its eye check (entity_fluid.rs:389-398) computes the top with world.camera_height(state, p) (fluid.rs:504 camera_height_at: a source fluid with a sturdy block above -> 1.0, else height_at). Observable: an entity whose eye is in (0.889, 1.0] above a source's block bottom with a solid ceiling -> the port says eyes-in-fluid, vanilla 26.1.2 says not; affects was_eye_in_water / is_under_water (swimming, overlay, air/drowning). The rest of the 26.3 form was verified behaviourally equivalent for vanilla fluids (flow scaling, fluid_height/is_in_fluid/is_eye_in_fluid, tracker pruning; the update bool return differs only in a 1mm band and all callers discard it). Reproduces 26.1.1 B1-G04.
items.title: Entity fluid interaction eye check uses camera height instead of the plain fluid top

items.evidence: RE-CHECKED FIRST. Vanilla 26.1.2 FlowingFluid.canHoldAnyFluid is hardcoded (javap-verified fresh, FlowingFluid.txt:1012-1075): LiquidBlockContainer -> true; blocksMotion -> false; excludes DoorBlock, #signs, ladder, sugar cane, bubble column, nether/end portals, end gateway, structure void; else true (air passes). Zero 'washed' references in FlowingFluid; washed_away_by_fluids does not exist in 26.1.2 data (no tag file, no BlockTags field, no prepared key). The port ships the 26.3 tag form (level/fluids.rs:359-361: is_liquid_container(state) || in_set(state, tags.washed_away_by_fluids), byte-identical to 26.1.1's), and Tags::resolve fills a missing tag with an empty set (level/data.rs:396), so can_hold_any_fluid is true only for liquid containers and NO fluid spreads at all, water or lava. The spread machinery itself is byte-identical to 26.1.1's verified code and matches vanilla - the failure is isolated to the predicate. Reproduces pilot G5 and 26.1.1 B1-G05.
items.title: NO fluid spreading at all, water or lava (canHoldAnyFluid reads the absent #washed_away_by_fluids tag)

items.evidence: Vanilla 26.1.2 LavaFluid.randomTick (javap-verified fresh): the first branch stops at the first blocksMotion() block (air + flammable neighbours -> set fire + return, else blocksMotion -> return, offset 188). blocks_lava_fire_spread does not exist in 26.1.2 data (no tag file, no BlockTags field, no prepared key). The port ships the 26.3 tag form (level/fluids.rs:777-785: tag("minecraft:blocks_lava_fire_spread").is_some_and(...), byte-identical to 26.1.1's), and BlockFacts::tag returns None for an absent tag (level/mod.rs:941), so the walk never stops at a solid block: fire spreads through stone, and the walk keeps drawing RNG after the first motion-blocking block, perturbing the random stream vs vanilla. The rest of lava_random_tick matches vanilla exactly. Reproduces pilot G3 and 26.1.1 B1-G06.
items.title: Lava fire spread walks through solid blocks (walk stops only for the absent #blocks_lava_fire_spread tag)

items.evidence: Vanilla 26.1.2 FlowingFluid.getFlow's below-check reads the per-state BlockState.blocksMotion() rule; there is no blocks_fluid_flow tag in 26.1.2 data (no tag file, no BlockTags field, no prepared key). The port ships the 26.3 tag form in both places (byte-identical to 26.1.1's): horizon-client-render/src/assets.rs:224-232 reads minecraft:blocks_fluid_flow from the prepared tag bundle (erroring if absent), and horizon-client/src/motion/fluids.rs:27-54 builds blocks_flow from the tag's BTreeSet<String>. fluid_flow::flow_at (horizon-world/src/fluid_flow.rs, byte-identical to 26.1.1's) then reads every neighbour as non-blocking, so flow vectors near solid blocks are computed as if the wall were not there - wrong push for entities, arrows, boats and mobs in water next to solids. Masked in practice by the Batch 3 startup blocker (MotionResources::load fails on the absent #causes_suffocation/#suppresses_bounce tags before the table is built). Reproduces 26.1.1 B1-G07; NEW vs 26.1.
items.title: Fluid-flow vector table reads the absent #blocks_fluid_flow tag (blocks_fluid_flow := blocks_motion mapping gone)

items.evidence: Vanilla 26.1.2 FallingBlockEntity.tick ends with deltaMovement.scale(0.98d) - the DOUBLE literal (ldc2_w // double 0.98d, offset 889, re-verified fresh). The port ships the 26.2 form (horizon-client/src/entity_rules.rs:11-14, byte-identical to 26.1.1's: let drag = f64::from(0.98_f32) = 0.9800000190734863), and the test was renamed to pin the wrong form (four_ticks_of_air_drag_match_vanilla_0_98f, expected bits 0x3fb7_9cd5_1b0c_538e vs 26.1's 0x3fb7_9cd4_fc35_0910). Effect: after 4 ticks 0.1 x 0.98^4 = 0.092236816 vs 0.1 x 0.98F^4 = 0.09223682318... - a ~7e-9 relative drift per tick, sub-mm over a full fall. Tiny but verified-wrong against the bytecode. scale_air_drag is shared with PrimedTnt.tick (out of scope). Reproduces 26.1.1 B1-G08; NEW vs 26.1.
items.title: Falling-block air drag uses 0.98F widened instead of the double literal 0.98

method: javap -c on the named 26.1.2 server-game jar (DataVersion 4790, protocol 775, Java 25) for every vanilla method in scope, plus Rust source comparison against versions/26.1.2/crates/ (including a full-tree diff vs the 26.1.1 tree, 34 files - none in scope - and a byte-identity check on all 35 in-scope files and all 13 in-scope oracle sources), tag/data reads from the 26.1.2 client jar and the 26.1.2 datagen reports (all five byte-identical to 26.1.1's), a measured per-class sha1 jar diff 26.1.1 vs 26.1.2 (server-game 3 classes changed, client 8, 0 added/removed; data changes are the 1,202 structure NBTs only), and oracle triage from the 26.1.1 Batch 0 table provisionally (the 26.1.2 table had not landed; every missing symbol javap-verified against the 26.1.2 jar). No prepared .local exists for 26.1.2 yet: prepared-data claims use the 26.1.1 prepare, justified by the jar-diff keystone, with both census vanilla sides counted fresh from 26.1.2's own jar/reports. No cargo builds, no unit tests, no fresh oracle measurement (brief constraints).
name: Fluids + falling blocks
out_of_scope_failures: None. Untraced sub-details (not counted as passes, not needs-harness): the lava-hurt GENERIC_BURN sound was not traced in the Rust; PointedDripstoneBlock.animateTick drip particles were not compared; dragon-egg teleport on use is out of scope (falling-block scope covers fall/landing/conversion) - though it was verified matching anyway (1000 tries, same offsets and gates). Oracle triage: 9 of the 13 in-scope oracles fail on all three classpaths (B1-O01..B1-O07); the other 4 pass (FluidBox, FluidOccupancy, FluidShape, WaterSplash - all three classpaths) - provisional on the 26.1.1 Batch 0 table until the 26.1.2 table lands; no verdict is expected to change. Out-of-scope observations flagged in the report (not B1 items): hooks.rs ice_destroyed_by_player + melt BLOCK_DESTROY event; game/campfire_douse.rs 26.3 form (#douses_campfires absent); worldgen/dripstone.rs maxOffset clamp; feature_world.rs heightmap tags; Assets::load missing-tag errors (render tests only); MotionResources missing motion tags (26.1 B3-G22 reproduces, Batch 3 scope); item-entity/TNT air-drag sharing the B1-G08 regression.
source: 26.1.2 parity sweep, batch 1 - the 1.21.7 pilot scope re-run against vanilla 26.1.2 (checks only, no fixes). Scope: water/lava spreading and flow, fluid pushing, bubble columns, concrete powder solidification, lava fire spread + ignition + game rules, dripstone growth + cauldron fill, falling blocks, cauldron fill levels, splash water. Re-checks all six 1.21.7 pilot defects (G1-G6) and Batch 11 findings B11-G06, B11-G13, plus all 17 items from the 26.1.1 run, against 26.1.2's own jar/data.
systemic_note: The 1.21.7 pilot's systemic root cause (26.x tag-based logic for tags absent in the target version's data) applies to 26.1.2 in the same FIVE places as 26.1.1: the speleothem system (B1-G01) and splash water (B1-G03) as in 26.1, PLUS three regressions where the 26.1.1 tree undid 26.1's fixes and the 26.1.2 tree inherits byte-identical - can_hold_any_fluid (B1-G05), the lava-fire walk (B1-G06), and the flow-vector table (B1-G07). A fourth regression is numeric: the falling-block air drag (B1-G08: 0.98F widened instead of the double literal). Unlike 26.1.1, the 26.1.2 tree is a genuine delta port (full-tree diff: 34 files, none in scope); vanilla itself changed nothing in scope (measured jar diff: only DetectedVersion, SharedConstants, ServerGamePacketListenerImpl in the server jar, plus Checkbox x3 and AbstractReportScreen x2 in the client jar), so every verdict is unchanged from 26.1.1 by construction. Where 26.1.2's data HAS the tag (bubble-column tags, #signs, #fire, #anvil, infiniburn), the port reads it; where 26.1.2 still lacks the tag, the port usually carries the hardcoded 1.21.7-style list form - except in the five places above, where it ships the 26.3 form. B1-G04 is the same pattern at a smaller scale (26.3-form entity fluid interaction, camera-height eye check).
